main_body: Three-storey red-brick building: a flat gravel/slate roof seen from above, a cream cornice, a brick facade with 3 rows of windows, and an arched green double door at the bottom
top_band: Roof surface of light grey-lilac L~168, with a highlighted back edge (L 226) and stone-slab speckle, rows 1-37 at x=80, ending in a light front-edge lip (L 189-235) at rows 38-40
evidence: The column at x=80 reads as a large lighter roof surface (rows 1-37, with chimney stacks and slab joints), then a light edge line at rows 38-40 (L 189-235). A cream cornice follows at rows 41-45 with a dark brick-red shadow row beneath it, then the brick front face with windows (cream lintels and sills, dark glass insets) down to the plinth. Both a roof top and a front face are clearly drawn. The roof is a flat deck rather than a pitched slope, but it is a visible horizontal surface. No receding side face. The windows are painted on a vertical face with sills and surrounds, so that is acceptable.

style.evidence: The measured facts show 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted: dark maroon beside brick and dark violet-grey beside the roof. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. The roof carries slab joints and speckle in about 5 steps (226, 181, 168, 158, 147, 125). The brick has several tones with per-course variation, and the windows have blue glazing with highlights. Median colours per tile are 12, which is above house-h112 (11) and a little below house-h101 (18). The total of 38 colours is lower than the references, but the piece is a repetitive facade. It would sit acceptably next to the references without looking sticker-like.
